sections.h2: Which written notices does a Maryland landlord have to give?
sections.html:
There are four main ones, and each has its own clock: a notice of intent to sue for unpaid rent, a breach notice, a notice that ends the tenancy, and a final notice of the eviction date. The reason for the eviction decides which one applies, and a defective notice can lead a court to dismiss a complaint or vacate a warrant.

SituationNotice and lengthAuthority
Unpaid rentWritten notice of intent to file, 10 days to payReal Property § 8-401
Lease violation, fixed-term lease30 days written notice§ 8-402.1
Violation showing clear and imminent danger14 days written notice§ 8-402.1
Ending a month-to-month tenancy or a written lease term over one week60 days§ 8-402
Ending a year-to-year tenancy90 days (180 for farm tenancies other than tobacco)§ 8-402
Ending a week-to-week tenancy7 days with a written lease, 21 days without§ 8-402
Warrant of restitution issuedAt least 6 days before the scheduled eviction§ 8-407

sections.h2: What does the 10-day nonpayment notice have to look like?
sections.html:
It must be on the Judiciary's form, which is DC-CV-115, and it gives the tenant 10 days to cure before the landlord may file. Section 8-401 allows delivery by certified first-class mail, by posting on the door, or electronically if the tenant chose that method, and electronic notice needs proof of transmission.

The landlord's sworn complaint must state the date the notice was given, and the court may dismiss a complaint on a showing of sufficient cause. The state's tenant guidance adds that only base rent counts toward the 10-day demand. Utility, maintenance and other charges do not. A landlord filing for more than the rent, such as a late fee, runs into a separate limit: late fees cannot exceed 5 percent of the late rent, and on a partial payment the fee can apply only to the unpaid portion.

sections.h2: What changes when the notice is about a lease violation?
sections.html:
The landlord has to wait 30 days after written notice that the tenant is in violation and that the landlord wants the property back. Section 8-402.1 applies to a lease with a fixed term that allows repossession for a breach, and the tenant or person in possession must refuse to comply.

Where the breach shows a clear and imminent danger of serious harm to people or property, the period drops to 14 days. A tenant who is ordered out can still appeal to the circuit court within 10 days of the judgment and stay in the home by filing an affidavit, posting a bond, paying back rent and court costs, and covering the landlord's losses from the holdover.

sections.h2: How much notice does a landlord give to end a tenancy without a violation?
sections.html:
Sixty days for most residential tenancies. Real Property § 8-402(c) sets 60 days for a month-to-month tenancy or a written lease for a stated term over one week, 90 days for year-to-year, and 7 or 21 days for week-to-week depending on whether a written lease exists.

A few related rules shape the timeline:

  • If the landlord receives a notice of intent to foreclose and wants to end the tenancy, the notice is at least 30 days for month-to-month or week-to-week tenancies and 60 days for year-to-year. This provision does not apply in Baltimore City or Montgomery County, to landlords with five or more residential units in the state, or to a property under a docketing order.
  • Accepting rent after notice does not waive the notice or a judgment unless the parties agree otherwise in writing.
  • A tenant who stays after the lease ends owes at least prorated rent at the lease rate for the holdover period.
  • A rent increase generally takes effect only at renewal and needs 90 days written notice, unless it is part of a notice to end the tenancy, according to the state's tenant bill of rights summary.

sections.h2: What must the final 6-day eviction notice say?
sections.html:
It must go out by three methods at once and carry a list of required details. Section 8-407 requires first-class mail with a certificate of mailing, a posting on the front door backed by a date-stamped photo, and email or text if the landlord has the tenant's address or number.

The notice has to include:

  • The court case number, the tenant's name as used in the case and the property address
  • The date the warrant was ordered and the initial eviction date
  • A statement that the eviction can be avoided by returning possession or, where available, by redeeming, with the amount due if redemption is still open
  • A statement that this is the final notice even if the eviction is delayed
  • A warning that belongings may be lost, a list of legal help resources, and the landlord's phone, email and mailing address

The landlord may charge the tenant no more than $5 for giving this notice. If the landlord hands the sheriff or constable the mailing certificate, a timestamped door photo and a signed affidavit from whoever posted it, notice is presumed proper, though a tenant can challenge that. If the sheriff doubts that notice was given, the warrant cannot be executed without a further court order. Local governments may set the notice period anywhere from 4 to 14 days.

sections.h2: Which notices and actions are off limits for a landlord?
sections.html:
Locking a tenant out and cutting off utilities are both banned. Under § 8-216, a landlord can take possession only through a warrant of restitution carried out by a sheriff or constable, or when the tenant has abandoned or surrendered the unit.

Section 8-208.1 also bars a landlord from suing for possession or ending a periodic tenancy because a tenant made a good-faith complaint, joined a tenants' group, took part in a lawsuit against the landlord, or called police or emergency services. The tenant can raise this as a defense or as a damages claim, with damages up to three months' rent plus fees. Retaliation relief generally requires the tenant to be current on rent, and anything done more than six months after the protected activity cannot be treated as retaliatory. The section contains no exception for a landlord who is selling.

sections.h2: What does a landlord owe a tenant when the house is being sold?
sections.html:
For a rental with three or fewer dwelling units, the owner generally has to offer the tenant a chance to buy before listing or marketing the home. Real Property § 8-119 gives that right to a named lessee who has occupied the property for at least six months.

The owner must mail a written notice on the form set by the Secretary of Housing and Community Development, by first-class mail with a certificate of mailing or a tracked delivery service, and send a copy to the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs. The tenant then has 30 days to deliver a written offer. If the offer matches the notice terms, the owner has 5 days to accept. A violation can bring a fine of up to $1,000.

The section lists transfers it does not cover, including:

  • Sales to a family member or to a business the owner wholly owns
  • Transfers by foreclosure, tax sale, court order or bankruptcy
  • Transfers by an estate, guardianship or trust fiduciary, or by will or inheritance

The state's tenant guidance also says a landlord may enter for showings to buyers on 24 hours written notice, generally Monday through Saturday between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. Properties with four or more units are outside the right of first refusal.

faqs.q: How many days notice must a Maryland landlord give before filing for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: Ten days. The landlord must use the Judiciary's form DC-CV-115, state the rent due, and give the tenant 10 days to pay before filing in District Court.

faqs.q: How long is a Maryland notice to end a month-to-month tenancy?
faqs.a: Sixty days. The landlord gives written notice at least 60 days before the tenancy ends. The tenant generally gives 30 days, unless the lease requires more.

faqs.q: Can a Maryland landlord evict someone with 14 days notice?
faqs.a: Only for a lease violation that shows a clear and imminent danger of serious harm to people or property. Other breach notices are 30 days.

faqs.q: Does a Maryland landlord have to give notice before the sheriff arrives?
faqs.a: Yes. After a warrant of restitution, the landlord must send written notice at least 6 days before the scheduled eviction by mail, posting and electronic message when contact details are known. Some local governments set 4 to 14 days.

faqs.q: Does a tenant get first chance to buy a rented Maryland house?
faqs.a: Often. A named tenant of at least six months in a property with three or fewer units has a right of first refusal, with exceptions for family transfers, foreclosure, estate transfers and a few others.

faqs.q: Does paying rent after a notice cancel the eviction?
faqs.a: Not on its own. Accepting payment after notice does not waive the notice or a judgment for possession unless the parties agree otherwise in writing.
